To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MAO‐catabolized products of l‐[11C]deprenyl are labeled with 11C at the α‐methyl position and that the retention of 11C in brain is dependent on the MAO‐mediated cleavage of the propargyl‐α carbon‐hydrogen bonds.

(a) MAO‐catabolism of the propargyl moiety of l‐deprenyI is the rate‐limiting step in the retention and binding of [11C]-l‐depreny I in brain and (b) the in vivo detection in brain of labeled products after the injection of l‐depre-nyl provides a record of the MAO‐cata-lyzed binding of this compound.
the deuterium isotopecffect in the MAO‐catabolism of [11C‐methylene‐2H2]l‐depneryl in living baboon brain has been measured to be 3.8.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a radiotracer that can be used to map MAO B in human and animal brains and with the development of methods to measure the kinetic properties of the radiotracer in vivo.
the development and application of positron emitting radioligands as tools for studying the biochemical processes in living animals and humans.
the development of positron‐emitting radiotracers for the study of enzyme kinetics and enzyme inhibition in the living brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deuterium isotopec effect in the metabolism of [11C]-l-deprenyl in the baboon brain is due to an isotope effect on the MAO-catalyzed α-carbon hydrogen cleavage.
the deuterium isosteric effect on the MAO‐catabolism of the propargyl moiety of l‐deprenyI in vivo has been demonstrated.
the carbon‐11 in the brain after injection of 11C‐labeled l-deprenyl is due to the MAO-catalyzed cleave of the carbon-hydrogen bond of l-depreny1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of [11C]-deprenyl as a radiotracter for mapping MAO-B in the living brain is a valid and useful approach, but that it must be used with caution.

the use of deuterium‐substituted tracers in mechanistic PET studies may allow the identification of the rate‐limiting steps in a metabolic process and may allow the measurement of the in vivo rate of a metabolic process in the brain.

the in vivo measurement of MAO activity in brain using [11C]deprenyl as a radiotracing agent is feasible and that the use of deuterium‐labeled [11C]‐deprenyl is an effective way to minimize the formation of [11C‐methamphetamine in brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the deuterium substitution in the α‐position of the propargyl moiety of l‐deprenyI significantly reduces the amount of radio‐activity bound to protein and increases the amount of [11C]-methamphetamine formed.
the use of deuterium‐labeled compounds as radiotracer probes can be a valuable tool in PET studies.
the use of deuterium‐labeled tracers is a valuable tool for studying the mechanism of enzyme‐mediated transformations of PET‐labeled tritium and carbon‐11 compounds in living animals.
